reason: '"Nobody answered." Three words.' "Nobody answered" is two words, and the story's lesson is about counting sentence length.

uncertain: 'In the mirror behind her, her bedroom door appeared on the right, but ... it was really on the left, because a mirror flips things.' A plane mirror reverses front-back, not left-right; the scene's geometry is unclear. The stage-left fact itself is stated correctly.

'Spontaneous combustion in the engine, right? That's what makes it go?' Marcus said yes... fuel burning all at once. A model rocket motor is lit by an electric igniter from a launch controller (per Estes/launch-controller guides), not spontaneous combustion, and its propellant burns over a second or two, not all at once. Lee Ross 1977 fact confirmed (Wikipedia, Fundamental attribution error).

'There's a winter league with January tryouts. New year, new cutoff. I'll be the old one for once.' With a January 1 cutoff a December-born player stays the youngest in his birth-year group whenever tryouts are held; the relative age effect depends on birth date relative to the cutoff, not on tryout timing.

'the little generator in the garage ... coughed to life ... the generator humming in the garage.' The CDC says never run a generator inside a home or garage, even with doors open, because of carbon monoxide; the story presents this as normal. Naismith fact is stated correctly.

'Four goals to two, which ... was the equivalent of a two-goal lead the whole second half.' Argentina led the 1930 final 2-1 at halftime and Uruguay scored three second-half goals (sources: goal.com, malaymail World Cup history). The injected fact is stated correctly.

uncertain: Lydia's plan to 'Carry my backpack' with her freshly broken, casted wrist goes unchallenged; doctors usually advise against lifting with a fractured wrist, though finger movement is encouraged.

'Six arms. Every single time.' / 'each one of them six-sided'. The fact says snowflakes almost always have six sides; triangular and twelve-sided snow crystals also occur (Libbrecht, Caltech snowcrystals.com).
'He had opened it five times.' The story shows him opening the fridge four times (first, 'again', 'And again', 'the fourth try'). USDA four-hour fact is stated correctly.
